findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and remain reusable
findings.body: The user-storage `isValid` branch for `recovery-authn-codes` only checks `anyMatch(key.equals(challengeResponse))` and never marks the code as used or removes it from the stored list. Combined with `getCredentials` rebuilding a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` from the raw list on every call, a recovery code accepted once stays valid forever and `allCodesUsed()` can never become true. This silently breaks the single-use contract of recovery codes for federated users (the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` consumes codes; the federated path introduced by this PR has no mechanism to do so). At minimum the test provider should consume the code so the test exercises realistic behaviour, and the production design should document/handle that `CredentialInputUpdater`-backed storages must consume codes themselves.

findings.title: Code number prompted to the user is always 0 when credential comes from user storage
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now prefers `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`. A model returned by a user storage (e.g. via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`) has no usage state, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` always yields code #0 and the login form keeps asking for the first code on every login. The new test even hard-codes `expectedCode == 0`, which masks this rather than catching it. The sequential-code UX is therefore lost for federated users without any error.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences possibly-null MyUser
findings.body: `getCredentials` calls `getMyUser(user)` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` / `myUser.otp` without a null check, unlike `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` in the same class. If `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is invoked for a user that is not (or no longer) in the in-memory map, this throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

findings.title: User label and generation timestamp are dropped when storing in user storage
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` passes only the raw code list (as JSON) to `updateCredential`; the `userLabel` and `generatedAt` values the user submitted (and that are stored in the local path via `credentialModel`) are not forwarded. The test provider consequently reads `getUserLabel()` which is always null. Storages cannot preserve the label, so the federated and local behaviour diverge for the same required action.

findings.title: No negative or fallback coverage for recovery codes in user storage
findings.body: The new test only verifies a single successful login with code #0. It does not verify that a used code is rejected on a second attempt, that an invalid code is rejected, that a second login prompts for the next code, or that a storage which does not support `recovery-authn-codes` falls back to local creation (the `else` branch in `createRecoveryCodesCredential`). The `delayed-authenticator` execution copied into the flow with delay 0 also adds nothing to the test.
